Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
A developer of a liquefied natural gas facility in Alaska received financing from Russia-based Novatek PJSC, an energy giant that is subject to US sanctions, the Financial Times reportedBloomberg Terminal
.
Novatek offered funding to Polar Train LNG’s venture and directed its operations before required approvals were secured from the US Treasury, the newspaper cited the developer’s ex-chief executive officer Joel Riddle as saying in an interview. Riddle resigned last month, followed by other executives, according to the FT and a separate interviewBloomberg Terminal
with the New York Times.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
India’s market regulator has ordered options trader Avadhut Sathe and his trading academy to refund 5.46 billion rupees ($57.5 million) to course participants after finding they provided unregistered investment advice and research services under the guise of stock market education.
In its final order, the Securities and Exchange Board of India also barred Sathe and Avadhut Sathe Trading Academy Pvt. from accessing the securities market for at least two years and directed them to pay 678.7 million rupees in interest.

Singapore expanded its investigation into haze-creating fires in Indonesia that have blanketed the city-state in smog, requesting information from 10 locally registered companies.
The National Environment Agency sent notices seeking documents and details of land concessions in Indonesia owned by the firms, their fire-fighting and blaze prevention measures, and their relationship to other relevant companies, according to a Friday statement.

The US has ordered the departure of diplomatic personnel and adjusted staffing at embassies across the Middle East as a result of Iranian efforts to target Americans, as well as threats from Houthi militants in Yemen, according to an American official.
The State Department had previously said the US was ordering some diplomatic staff to depart only from Saudi Arabia as a result of the growing risk from the Houthis, but had called reports of broader US evacuations across the Middle East “inaccurate.”

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Growth and value shares are set for an overhaul after S&P Dow Jones Indices adopted new rules on how to sort equities into the two investment styles.
The index provider will add intangible assets, forward earnings and free cash flow to the list of factors to define whether a company is cheap relative to its share price, according to a statement Friday. At the same time, 12-month price momentum will be dropped as a criteria to rank a company’s growth potential.

item.title: Andrew Brandt on MLB Salary Cap Fight as World Series Begins
item.description:
Oct 23rd, 2026
Andrew Brandt on MLB Salary Cap Fight as World Series Begins
Andrew Brandt says the Brewers and Rays reaching the World Series—despite ranking 19th and 26th in payroll, respectively—shows how strong management, scouting and player development can compete with high spending. He calls the matchup evidence for the players’ union that success is possible without a salary cap, while cautioning that owners may dismiss it as an unsustainable exception: smaller-market teams have little margin for error and can lose players to wealthier clubs in free agency. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close."
